claim_support.claim: The incident narrative describes a confirmed failure of the device to flag a clinically significant complete atrioventricular block (a safety-critical event) in real-time.
Crucially, this miss has been observed in two separate patients on the same software version, establishing recurrence across the deployed population.
This pattern indicates a systemic defect with serious potential for patient harm (missed detection of life-threatening arrhythmia).
The narrative explicitly states 'recurrence across the deployed population,' which triggers obligations under vigilance and field safety corrective action frameworks rather than simple internal CAPA.

However, confidence is reduced to 0.58 because no specific technical artifact (e.g., a relevant test log showing the classifier failure or code diff identifying the root cause) was retrieved; all provided static analysis logs are explicitly labeled as 'unrelated' distractors.

The judgment relies entirely on the narrative description of the clinical event and recurrence, which is insufficient for full confidence in the specific technical mechanism without corroborating engineering data.
